subject: Request: threshold-split credit sanction for MedForge pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@medforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot commercial proposal and onboarding structure

Elaine — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a starter commercial outline and SOW draft for the 6‑month pilot (attached). Key points: 1) pilot pricing at $0.035/token for production calls, 2) onboarding credit of $30k applied against first invoice, 3) standard SLA and data controls.

You mentioned procurement would want a deeper first‑year credit and a firmness on consumption forecasts — happy to discuss. If MedForge can commit to a 12‑month consumption corridor after the pilot we can layer in additional credits. Sending for visibility to Marissa and Markus for any immediate constraints.

Attachments: MedForge_MATP_v5_redlines.pdf (proposal redlines), SOW-Redwood-onboarding-draft.docx

Best,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555‑0192

From: Elaine Park <elaine@medforge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commercial proposal and onboarding structure

Sean — thanks, received. A few quick asks from procurement/finance here:
- MedForge needs a 35% effective first‑year discount to justify running a parallel pilot (budget constraints).
- They want a usage floor guarantee tied to a "threshold split": if monthly usage falls below the floor, Redwood provides a pro‑rated credit to make the economics whole for MedForge.
- Procurement asked that the onboarding credit be elevated to $75k or converted into service credits (we prefer cash offset).

I can push them down toward a 30% if you can offer more committed minimums, but procurement said anything under 30% will likely get rejected. Can you confirm final flexibility and who on your side signs off on a >25% concession?

—Elaine
Director of Cloud Ops, MedForge
procurement@medforge.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T13:08:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: MedForge asks — need authorization path (>25% concession)

Marissa/Markus — forwarding MedForge's asks above. TL;DR: procurement wants 35% first‑year effective discount, a threshold split credit if usage misses the floor, and $75k onboarding cash offset. The opportunity is strategic: MedForge is a mid‑market medical analytics provider with potential to scale quickly across 3 product lines (estimated 2–3x volume in year two).

My recommendation: approve a conditional 30% effective first‑year concession with a 12‑month minimum commitment (ARR floor of $450k) + $50k onboarding credit (cash offset), and formalize the threshold split as a 60/40 usage shortfall split (Redwood covers 60% of the shortfall credit). That preserves economics while addressing MedForge's procurement ask.

If leadership can approve or provide a counter (e.g., 28% + $60k credit), I can close quickly — procurement wants exec‑level confirmation. Please advise path to VP/CFO signoff for anything >25%.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MedForge asks — need authorization path (>25% concession)

Sean — I reviewed the ask. A few comments:
- 35% is outside our standard commercial guardrails for this cohort unless there is a multi‑year commitment with clear price floors.
- I like your conditional approach. Approve up to 20% first‑year effective discount without exec signoff. Anything between 21–30% requires VP signoff; above 30% requires CFO signoff.
- Onboarding cash: we can stretch to $50k cash offset + $25k professional services credits (total value $75k) but prefer credits vs. cash.
- Threshold split proposal: propose Redwood covers 50% of the shortfall credit (not 60%) and cap our exposure at $75k for the pilot period.

Please prepare a concise memo to markus@redwood.com and marissa@redwood.com that states the requested concession, economic impact (net present value of credits vs committed ARR), and ask for VP/CFO signoff. Include the SOW and the redlined contract so execs can sign off quickly.

Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@medforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commercial proposal and onboarding structure

Elaine — quick update: we reviewed your ask internally and are preparing an exec memo for final approval. For speed, here's a working offer I can present to your procurement: 1) 28% effective first‑year discount, 2) threshold split where Redwood covers 50% of monthly shortfall credits up to a $75k cap over the pilot, 3) onboarding value of $75k delivered as $50k cash offset + $25k PS credits, 4) a 12‑month firm commitment post‑pilot with a $450k minimum.

I'm attaching the updated SOW and redlines. We need an acceptance or a confirmation of the commitment corridor by end of week to get this to execs for signoff.

Attachments: MedForge_MATP_v5_redlines.pdf, SOW-Redwood-onboarding-draft.docx

Best,
Sean

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MedForge asks — need authorization path (>25% concession)

Sean/Marissa — reviewed the memo and modeled the economics. Approved with conditions:
- Final concession: 28% effective first‑year discount (approved by VP sales + CFO authority exercised).
- Threshold split: Redwood covers 50% of shortfall credit, capped at $75k for the pilot.
- Onboarding: $50k cash offset + $25k professional services credits (as proposed).
- Condition: MedForge executes the 12‑month post‑pilot commitment with a $450k minimum within 30 days of pilot completion; otherwise, Redwood reserves right to invoice full listed rates retroactively (minus provided credits).

I will sign the exception memo and route to finance/corp legal for the DocuSign packet. Sean — proceed to confirm with MedForge and get a procurement signed acceptance.

Markus Klein
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
